advances: Counterexample to the auxiliary basin inequality under finite grouped-cap geometry. The common budget exceeds the sharp Oertel target $gamma_2M/4$, and the contacts are in the auxiliary complementary polytope, outside the source body.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let the base polygon be given by $z_1,z_2\ge0$, $|z_1-z_2|\le1$, $z_1+z_2\le3$. Its vertices are $(0,0),(1,0),(2,1),(1,2),(0,1)$ and its lattice points add only $(1,1)$, as can be read from the displayed sum and difference bounds. At the six lattice bases take squares centered at $b(z)=(11-4z_1-4z_2,4z_1-5)$. Let their radius in the infinity norm be $1/10$ at $(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)$ and $1/100$ at the other three bases. Take the convex hull of the six lifted squares. It is bounded and full-dimensional since the projection spans $\mathbb R^2$ and a square spans the two fiber directions. Projection extremality fixes the five vertex fibers. At $(1,1)$ every convex combination has the center prescribed by the affine map $b$ and displacement of infinity norm at most $1/10$. Thus all six prescribed fibers are actual. Each large square has area $1/25$, and each small square has area $1/2500$.

The four binary roots are fixed under the parity midpoint map and both nonroots map to $(1,1)$. Write $B$ for its basin, the three large fibers. Take continuous normals $u_1=(1,0)$, $u_2=(0,1)$, $u_3=(-1,-1)$ in every group. Their minimal positive dependence has coefficients $1/3$ and rank two. Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell_{00}(z)&=1/100-(z_1+z_2)/10,&
\ell_{10}(z)&=(z_1-z_2)/10-1/20,\\
\ell_{01}(z)&=(z_2-z_1)/10-1/20,&
\ell_{11}(z)&=(z_1+z_2)/10-1/10.
\end{aligned}
$$
The caps are $H_{s,j}=\{(z,x):u_j\cdot x+\ell_s(z)\ge0\}$. The complementary polytope uses all twelve reversed weak inequalities. Summing the three inequalities for each group shows that its projection lies in $1/10\le z_1+z_2\le1$, $|z_1-z_2|\le1/2$. Conversely $x=0$ works at every point of this region. Each coordinate lies in $[-1/5,3/4]$ there, and $(0,0)$ is excluded by the sum lower bound, so there is no integer base. Positive spanning of the continuous normals gives bounded fibers uniformly over this bounded projection: for any one group, the two coordinate upper bounds and a lower bound on their sum bound both coordinates. At $z=(11/40,11/40),x=0$ all inequalities are strict.

The common real contacts have continuous coordinate zero and base coordinates $(1/20,1/20)$, $(5/8,1/8)$, $(1/8,5/8)$ and $(1/2,1/2)$ in group order $00,10,01,11$. At each of them its own $\ell_s$ vanishes and the other three are strictly negative by substitution. Writing $\ell_s(z)=a_s\cdot z-h_s$, expand the offsets to $\beta_s=0,1/10,1/10,1/5$ in group order. Then $\beta_s>h_s$ for every group. The expanded projected region has $0\le z_1+z_2\le2$, $|z_1-z_2|\le1$. Each binary root is on its own row and strictly satisfies the other rows; both nonroots violate the expanded upper sum bound. Thus no sampled base is in its interior, and the four strict exclusive facet witnesses have all four parities.

The three large centers, in order $(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)$, are $(3,-1),(-1,3),(-1,-1)$. Across all groups and bases the common terms are between $-29/100$ and $1/5$. The intended continuous normal $u_1,u_2,u_3$, respectively, gives at least $18/10$ before adding the common term throughout its square, and each unintended continuous normal gives at most $-9/10$. Hence each large square is strictly inside only its assigned cap in each group. The three small centers $(11,-5),(7,-1),(7,-5)$ and their $1/100$ radii place the small squares strictly inside cap 1 and outside caps 2 and 3 in every group. This proves the stated cap masses and the group cover. Finally $\mu(B)=3/25$, and $(4/9)(3/25)-103/2500=91/7500$.

source_sections.locator: d0f838592db846be:03 A six-fiber full-parity example through Exact failure of basin mass promotion, (3)–(6)

statement:
There is a full-dimensional mixed-integer body in $\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^2$ with six positive-area fibers and a grouped closed-cap certificate with the following properties. Four binary roots occupy the four parities, expose their respective strict expanded-facet rows, and determine the midpoint map $z\mapsto\lceil z/2\rceil$ coordinatewise. Each group has a rank-two minimal positive dependence of three continuous normals and a common real contact in the bounded full-dimensional mixed-integer-free complementary polytope. All other groups are strict at that contact.

The root $(1,1)$ has a three-fiber basin of mixed mass $3/25$ entirely covered by its own group. All four groups have the same respective cap masses $103/2500,100/2500,100/2500$, strictly below the common budget $104/2500$. The maximum cap mass of the $(1,1)$ group is therefore smaller than $\gamma_2$ times its basin mass by $91/7500$, where $\gamma_2=4/9$ and the total original mass is $303/2500$.
title: Full-parity cap circuits do not promote basin mass by the Grünbaum factor
